title: Provision and remove staff
statement: Approve each staff member's access before adding them, change it when their job changes, and deactivate them in OpenClear (or in the bank's identity provider) by the bank's own deadline when they leave.
complements: OpenClear grants only what a person's security group allows, records every membership change in the action log, and stops a deactivated person signing in or using a token at once.
where: Users → Export (with last sign-in); user.* and membership.* in the action log

title: Keep the identity provider in step
statement: When staff sign on through the bank's identity provider, keep its group mapping and SCIM provisioning in step with the bank's directory, so someone disabled there is disabled in OpenClear.
complements: OpenClear applies SCIM deactivations and group changes as they arrive, and refuses a sign-on the identity provider refuses.
where: Settings → Sign-on; scim.* in the action log

title: Review staff access
statement: At least quarterly, review each staff member's security group, customer scope and account access, remove what's no longer needed, and record the review.
complements: OpenClear exports every membership with its group, scope, account access and last sign-in, and records each change.
where: Users → Export; the access review record (CT3)

title: Give the least access a job needs
statement: Decide who holds admin permissions and keep them few; use customer scope and per-account access where a role is narrower than the whole bank; don't give day-to-day deciders admin permissions.
complements: OpenClear checks every request against the person's permissions, scope and account access.

title: Separate conflicting duties
statement: Design security groups so no group combines conflicting duties, then move segregation of duties from warn to enforce.
complements: OpenClear checks groups against the bank's conflict rules, refuses a breach under enforce (ERR_SOD_VIOLATION) and logs it under either mode, and never lets whoever presented an item decide it.
where: Settings → Segregation of duties; Controls; sod.violation in the action log

title: Use dual control on decisions
statement: Turn on dual control for pay/return decisions where the bank's policy needs a second person, and staff it so a checker is available before every cutoff.
complements: OpenClear holds a recommended decision until a different person approves it, and records both.
where: Settings → Decisions; decision histories in the evidence export

title: Approve rule and model changes
statement: Have a second admin approve every change to matching rules and scoring models, and approve only changes the bank has assessed.
complements: Under enforce, OpenClear holds a rule or model change until another admin approves it, and records both people.
where: Settings → Changes; the evidence export's changes

title: Replay before changing rules
statement: Before approving a matching-rule or model change, replay recent presented-item files through it at Model risk and review the variance report.
complements: OpenClear's replay runs the real matching code in a dry run that's rolled back, and keeps the report.
where: Settings → Model risk; control runs in the evidence export

title: Second factor for admins
statement: Make everyone who can change who may do what sign in with a security key or passkey, or only through the bank's identity provider with a second factor there.
complements: OpenClear supports FIDO2 security keys and passkeys, and SSO-only sign-in per bank, and reports admins without either.
where: Controls → Admins use a second factor

title: Second factor for staff
statement: Require a second factor (a security key or passkey, or the bank's identity provider) of everyone who can decide exceptions or change data; a bank under New York DFS Part 500 (500.12, from November 2025) requires it of every person who signs in.
complements: OpenClear supports FIDO2 security keys and passkeys, and SSO-only sign-in per bank.

title: Second factor at the identity provider
statement: Have the bank's identity provider (and any customer's the bank allows) require a second factor for everyone who signs in to OpenClear through it.
complements: People who sign in through single sign-on are exempt from OpenClear's own security-key requirement, which relies on this; a connection can be set to refuse a sign-in the provider doesn't report as multi-factor.
where: Settings → Sign-on (Require the identity provider to report MFA)

title: Second factor in online banking
statement: Have the online banking site that shows OpenClear inside its pages sign its users in with a second factor.
complements: An embedded session is started by the online banking site for a user it has already signed in, so it's exempt from OpenClear's own security-key requirement.

title: Set the password policy
statement: When password sign-in is on, set the password policy (length, character rules, lockout) to the bank's own standard.
complements: OpenClear enforces the bank's password policy and locks an account after repeated failures.
where: Settings → Password policy; tenant.* in the action log

title: Look after integration credentials
statement: Rotate API client secrets at least yearly (or use key pairs), keep them in the bank's secret store, and revoke a client when its system is retired.
complements: OpenClear shows each secret only once, stores only its hash, supports private_key_jwt, and reports secrets over a year old.
where: Settings → API clients; Controls → Integration secrets rotated

title: Grant support access with care
statement: Grant the platform's support staff access only for a stated reason and period, approve write access only when it's needed, and review each grant.
complements: OpenClear gives support staff no access to a bank except what the bank grants, under their own name, ending on time.
where: Settings → Support access; support_access.* in the action log

title: Verify customers' administrators
statement: Verify who a business customer's administrators are, and their authority to act for the customer, before giving them access or letting the customer manage its own people.
complements: OpenClear gives a customer's people access only through the bank, or through administrators the bank has set up.
where: Customers → People; customer.* in the action log

title: Let customers manage themselves with care
statement: Let a customer manage its own people or sign-on only after verifying its administrators, and make sure each customer that manages its own people has one.
complements: OpenClear limits a self-managing customer to its own people, accounts and the roles the bank offers.

title: Set how customers sign in
statement: Decide how each business customer's people must sign in (password policy, second factor, the customer's own identity provider) and set it.
complements: OpenClear enforces each customer's password policy, second factors and sign-on connection.

title: Cover OpenClear in written policies
statement: Cover positive pay in the bank's cybersecurity policies (vendor management, incident response and notification, access control) and its written information security program, and approve them each year (23 NYCRR 500.3; for Massachusetts residents' information, 201 CMR 17.03).
complements: OpenClear's controls and CUECs say what it does and what it relies on the bank for.
csf: GV.OC-03; GV.PO-01; GV.PO-02; GV.OV-01; GV.SC-03; ID.IM-01; ID.IM-02; ID.IM-03

title: Support the annual certification
statement: Keep the evidence exports and host attestations that support the bank's annual cybersecurity certification (for New York DFS, by April 15, 23 NYCRR 500.17(b)) for five years.
complements: OpenClear's evidence export is signed, and its host attestations are recorded.

title: Inventory OpenClear
statement: List OpenClear and its host in the bank's asset inventory, with an owner, the data's classification and a recovery time before the decision cut-off (23 NYCRR 500.13).
complements: OpenClear lists the outside services turned on, and the evidence export records the version running.

title: Know which accounts are consumer accounts
statement: Identify each account on OpenClear that is a consumer account under Regulation E, and apply the bank's Regulation E procedures to it alongside positive pay, and meet any duty under the CFPB's personal financial data rights rule (12 CFR 1033) for it through the bank's own interfaces.
complements: OpenClear protects business and consumer accounts the same way, and its decision history shows when an item was shown, decided and by whom.

title: Assess positive pay risk
statement: Include OpenClear in the bank's risk assessment and in the information security program's yearly report to the board (12 CFR 364 App. B III.F), and set each customer's services and default dispositions from it.
complements: OpenClear applies each customer's services and default dispositions as set.

title: Keep the check-fraud controls positive pay doesn't provide
statement: Keep account opening and monitoring, kiting detection and stop payments in the bank's own program and the core.
complements: OpenClear catches checks that weren't issued, altered amounts and payees, duplicates and a check cashed at a branch, but sees nothing of how an account was opened or of money moving between accounts.
csf: GV.RM-06; GV.RM-07; GV.SC-03; GV.SC-09; GV.SC-10; ID.AM-05; ID.RA-01; ID.RA-03; ID.RA-04; ID.RA-05; ID.IM-01; ID.IM-02; ID.IM-03; DE.AE-06; DE.AE-07; RS.AN-08

title: Offboard customers that leave
statement: When a customer leaves the bank or stops positive pay, set its last service day in OpenClear, stop the core sending its items, and keep the records the bank must keep in the core, which is the system of record.
complements: OpenClear ends the customer's sign-in and refuses its accounts' items after the last service day, and deletes its data 90 days later with a signed certificate, unless it's on legal hold.
where: Customers → a customer's Offboarding; Customers → Deleted customers

title: Keep custom fields to what positive pay needs
statement: Define custom fields on customers and accounts only for what the service needs (identifiers, codes), never a taxpayer id, a password or personal data with no use here; mark a field shown to the customer only when the customer should see it; and review the fields yearly.
complements: OpenClear limits fields to 25 per kind, records every definition and value change with before and after, shows a customer only fields marked for it, and says what not to store on the page where fields are defined.
where: Settings → Custom fields; the action log

title: Screen for sanctions where the money moves
statement: Screen accountholders, people cashing checks, payees where the bank's risk assessment calls for it, and inbound IAT parties for OFAC sanctions in the core, teller and ACH systems. A pay decision in OpenClear isn't an OFAC clearance.
complements: OpenClear doesn't screen for sanctions. It shows the payee as issued, as read from the image and as typed at a branch, so a bank can check one when it has reason to.

title: Protect downloads on the bank's devices
statement: Encrypt laptops and portable media that hold OpenClear exports, decision files or check images, and keep such files off unmanaged devices (201 CMR 17.04(5)).
complements: OpenClear records each export and download in the action log.

title: Govern the scoring model
statement: Before turning fraud scoring on, inventory the bank's model under its model-risk or AI policy, tier it and name an owner; while it's on, review its metrics, champion/challenger record and replays at least yearly, and turn it off if they degrade.
complements: OpenClear keeps scoring off until the bank turns it on, activates a model only after 200 of the bank's own decisions, learns only from decisions people made, and shows each model's metrics and how it was chosen.
csf: GV.RM-06; GV.RM-07; GV.SC-03; GV.SC-09; GV.SC-10; ID.AM-05; ID.RA-01; ID.RA-03; ID.RA-04; ID.RA-05; ID.IM-01; ID.IM-02; ID.IM-03; DE.AE-06; DE.AE-07; RS.AN-08

title: Set retention and disposal
statement: Decide how long positive pay records (issued checks, items, images, decisions) are kept and how they're disposed of, and at exit obtain the host's record that the bank's data was deleted (12 CFR 364 App. B II.B.4, III.C.4).
complements: OpenClear keeps a bank's business records until the bank leaves; then, after the bank is told and a wait, it deletes them and signs a certificate whose action-log hash lets the bank check its final export is complete.
where: Settings → Data export; the deletion certificate

title: Act on control status
statement: Watch control status (the Controls page, the API, or control.status.changed in the SIEM) and investigate a WARN or FAIL by the bank's own deadline.
complements: OpenClear tests its controls hourly and raises a security event when one changes.

title: Run the anomaly-capture test
statement: Turn on the daily anomaly-capture test, and investigate any synthetic fraud it misses.
complements: OpenClear's anomaly-capture test runs injected fraud through the bank's live rules in a dry run and records what was caught.
csf: ID.RA-01; ID.RA-07; ID.IM-01; ID.IM-02; ID.IM-03; DE.CM-01; DE.CM-02; DE.CM-03; DE.CM-06; DE.CM-09; DE.AE-02; DE.AE-03
where: Settings → Model risk; Controls → Synthetic fraud caught

nist_title: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
title: Review security events and the action log
statement: Send OpenClear's security events to the bank's SIEM (or read them through the API), alert on the ones that matter to the bank, and review the action log for unusual activity.
complements: OpenClear records every state-changing action in a signed, hash-chained log, and delivers security events in order and at least once.
where: Settings → Security event forwarding; Controls → Security events delivered

title: Keep the evidence
statement: Take an evidence export at least quarterly and keep it, with the action log's archives, for as long as the bank's retention schedule requires, in storage the bank controls; under New York DFS Part 500 (500.6), keep decision records five years and security events three, in the bank's SIEM, since OpenClear keeps security events 30 days by default.
complements: OpenClear's evidence export is signed, so it can be checked years later without OpenClear.

title: Decide every exception in time
statement: Staff the exception queue so every exception is decided, by the customer or the bank, before its deadline.
complements: OpenClear raises exceptions with their deadline, reminds before the cutoff, and applies the default disposition to anything left undecided.

where: Controls → Decisions and imports on time

title: Monitor incoming ACH credits for fraud
statement: Run, and review at least yearly, the bank's own risk-based process to identify incoming ACH credits initiated by fraud, as the Nacha Rules require of every RDFI from 2026.
complements: OpenClear's ACH positive pay monitors debits only and isn't that process; its evidence export summarizes debits, exceptions and returns for the bank's fraud-monitoring file.

title: Treat an unauthorized consumer return as a notice of error
statement: When a consumer account's ACH debit is returned as unauthorized through OpenClear, treat it as the consumer's notice under Regulation E and meet the investigation, provisional-credit and reporting times in 12 CFR 1005.11.
complements: OpenClear records the decision, its reason, who made it and when, with notes and images, in the evidence and data exports.

title: Return late unauthorized consumer debits on time
statement: For a consumer debit reported unauthorized after OpenClear's decision, return it by the opening of the sixth banking day after the bank finishes reviewing the signed Written Statement of Unauthorized Debit.
complements: OpenClear decides debits before they post; a late claim is the bank's, through its core.

title: Name incident contacts
statement: Name at least one incident contact in OpenClear, with the CEO and CIO as the fallback, keep them current, and confirm them each year.
complements: OpenClear sends the service provider's incident notices to them, and warns while there are none or they're a year old.

title: Notify the FDIC within 36 hours
statement: Decide whether an incident involving OpenClear is a notification incident and, if so, notify the FDIC supervisory office as soon as possible and within 36 hours of that determination (12 CFR 304.23).
complements: OpenClear's incident notice gives the bank the facts and when it was told, recorded with its acknowledgement.

title: Notify New York DFS within 72 hours
statement: A bank supervised by New York DFS notifies DFS within 72 hours of determining that a cybersecurity incident occurred at OpenClear's host, and updates DFS with material new information (23 NYCRR 500.17(a)).
complements: OpenClear's incident notice gives the bank the facts and when it was told.
csf: PR.IR-03; RS.MA-01; RS.MA-02; RS.MA-03; RS.MA-04; RS.AN-06; RS.AN-07; RS.CO-02; RS.CO-03; RC.CO-03

title: Report check fraud to FinCEN, and keep SARs out of OpenClear
statement: Decide and file suspicious activity reports for check fraud by the bank's own procedure, using OpenClear's records as supporting documentation (with the key term FIN-2023-MAILTHEFT where it applies), and never record in OpenClear that a SAR was or wasn't filed (31 CFR 1020.320(e)).
complements: OpenClear keeps the victim-side facts a narrative needs (as issued, as presented, images, decisions, branch attempts) and has no field for a SAR; customer users and support staff can read notes and reasons.

title: Obtain and keep Written Statements of Unauthorized Debit
statement: Obtain a Written Statement of Unauthorized Debit from a customer who reports a consumer ACH debit as unauthorized, as the Nacha Rules require, and keep it for the period they set.
complements: OpenClear shows customers the bank's own statement form (Markdown, HTML or a PDF) and warns while a bank that returns consumer debits has none published.
csf: PR.IR-03; RS.MA-01; RS.MA-02; RS.MA-03; RS.MA-04; RS.AN-06; RS.AN-07; RS.CO-02; RS.CO-03; RC.CO-03

title: Scan files for malware
statement: Use commercially standard malware detection on the computers and systems that send files to OpenClear, and on files staff download from it.
complements: OpenClear accepts only the file types it reads, re-encodes images, and can check every upload with ClamAV and VirusTotal's hash lookups, refusing malware and quarantining a file found later (both optional).
where: Settings → Outside services (malware scanning); file.malware_detected in the action log

title: Put loss allocation in the positive pay agreement
statement: Agree in writing with each positive pay customer the cut-off, the default decision, that undecided items follow it, the customer's duty to send issue files before checks are presented and to review exceptions, and how loss falls if it doesn't (UCC 4-103), and have counsel confirm it under the state's UCC.
complements: OpenClear records the settings the agreement names, and for each item when it was raised, shown, decided and by whom.
where: Customers → Default decision; Settings → Decision cut-off

title: Return checks in time
statement: Set cut-offs so the core can send every return before the midnight deadline and Regulation CC's expeditious-return time (12 CFR 229.31(b)), and give notice of nonpayment for returns of $5,000 or more (229.31(c)) from the core.
complements: OpenClear keeps each check's decision deadline within its midnight deadline, counted from the day it was presented, and flags a decision sent after it.
where: Settings → Decision cut-off; Controls → Checks decided within their return deadline

title: Tell OpenClear the bank's banking days
statement: Record the days the bank is closed, and whether it opens on the Federal Reserve's holidays, so deadlines follow the bank's banking days.
complements: OpenClear counts a check's return deadline in the bank's banking days.

title: Keep decision records for disputes
statement: Keep exception, decision and image records at least as long as UCC claims can be brought (at least a year, UCC 4-406(f)), plus any litigation hold.
complements: OpenClear keeps every decision, its revisions and the action log, signed, and exports them.

title: Connect the core
statement: Agree and document the interface with the core system (presented items in, decisions out), and confirm decisions are applied in the core before its cutoff.
complements: OpenClear delivers decisions through the decision outbox, retries, and reports a late or failing delivery.
where: Settings → Decision delivery; Controls → Decisions and imports on time

title: Reconcile presented items
statement: Reconcile each presented-items file OpenClear loads (its item count and total) against what the core sent, and investigate a difference. A posted-check layout that names the file's trailer does this for you; reconcile the files without one yourself.
complements: OpenClear stores each file with its SHA-256 and a signature, and reports the items and total it loaded. A file read by a posted-check layout with a trailer is refused whole, and raised as a security event, when its lines don't add up to the trailer.

title: Agree reverse positive pay in writing
statement: Before putting a customer's account on reverse positive pay, agree it in writing with the customer, including that every check they don't return by the cut-off is paid, and keep the agreement.
complements: OpenClear puts an account on reverse positive pay only as a protected change, and lists the accounts on it and those put on it in the last 30 days.

title: Set the teller fallback
statement: Decide what the teller platform does when OpenClear doesn't answer a verification in time (for example, decline above an amount), configure it in the teller platform, and train tellers on it.
complements: OpenClear answers a verification quickly and says plainly when a check can't be cashed, but can't enforce what a teller does when it can't be reached.

title: Plan for an outage at the cutoff
statement: Include positive pay in the bank's business continuity plan: what happens to exceptions and decisions if OpenClear or the core is unavailable at the cutoff, and who decides by hand.
complements: OpenClear applies each account's default disposition to undecided exceptions, and keeps the decisions to send once the core is back.

title: Exercise the cutoff outage plan
statement: Exercise B-CP-2-01's plan at least yearly, including getting pay and return decisions to the core before the return deadline without OpenClear, check the bank's recovery objectives against the host's, and record the result.
complements: OpenClear shows the host's recovery objectives and last restore test on the Controls page.

title: Train the deciders
statement: Train staff who decide exceptions (fraud red flags, return deadlines and reasons, when to call the customer) before they get access, and each year.
complements: OpenClear shows the information a decision needs, but can't judge whether the person deciding has been trained.

title: Handle incidents involving OpenClear
statement: Include OpenClear in the bank's incident response plan, keep the bank's incident contacts current with whoever hosts it, and report incidents involving it as the bank's rules require, notifying customers and the FDIC as 12 CFR 364 App. B Supplement A requires even when the unauthorized access was at the host.
complements: OpenClear's action log, security events and evidence export reconstruct who did what, and when.

title: Check accessibility against the bank's obligations
statement: Compare OpenClear's accessibility statement with the bank's own ADA and policy obligations, and report any barrier the bank's staff or customers meet.
complements: OpenClear checks WCAG 2.2 A and AA automatically on every build, and states what isn't yet checked.

title: Write OpenClear into the third-party policy
statement: Assess OpenClear and its host under the bank's third-party service provider policy before use and periodically, with a contract covering access controls and multi-factor sign-in, encryption, notice of cybersecurity events affecting the bank or unauthorized access to its customers' information, representations and warranties, and deletion at exit (23 NYCRR 500.11; 12 CFR 364 App. B III.D; 201 CMR 17.03(2)(f)).
complements: OpenClear supplies the controls, CUECs, host attestations, security metrics and evidence export a contract and an assessment rely on.

title: Tell the FDIC about the service relationship
statement: Notify the FDIC of the relationship with OpenClear's host within 30 days of the contract or the first service, whichever is first (Bank Service Company Act § 7(c)).
complements: OpenClear's documentation names the services it performs, for the notice to describe.

title: Evaluate OpenClear as an externally developed application
statement: Review OpenClear's security evidence (the ASVS crosswalk, the threat model, advisories and each release's security metrics) each year and before a major upgrade (23 NYCRR 500.8).
complements: OpenClear publishes them with each release.

title: Assess the outside services turned on
statement: Assess each outside service the bank turns on (email and SMS providers, cloud OCR, object storage, identity providers, a hosting provider) as a third party, and review it each year.
complements: OpenClear turns no outside service on by itself, and shows which ones are on.

title: Secure the bank's integrations
statement: Point webhooks and decision delivery at HTTPS endpoints on the bank's systems, and check each webhook's signature before acting on it.
complements: OpenClear signs every webhook, and delivers only to a public HTTPS address.

title: Manage the customer's own people
statement: When the customer manages its own people, add only people it has approved, change their role when their job changes, and deactivate them the day they leave.
complements: OpenClear keeps a customer's people to its own accounts and to the roles the bank offers, and records every change.

title: Tell the bank about joiners and leavers
statement: When the bank manages the customer's people, tell the bank promptly when someone joins, changes role or leaves.
complements: OpenClear removes a person's access as soon as the bank deactivates them.

title: Run the customer's identity provider
statement: When the customer's people sign on through its own identity provider, require a second factor there and disable leavers there.
complements: OpenClear accepts only the customer's verified email domains from its identity provider, and applies SCIM changes as they arrive.

title: Review the customer's access
statement: At least quarterly, review who in the customer can see and decide its items, and remove what's no longer needed.
complements: OpenClear lists the customer's people with their role, accounts and last sign-in.

title: Separate issuing from deciding
statement: Where the customer's size allows, keep apart the people who issue checks or upload issue files and the people who decide exceptions.
complements: OpenClear never lets the person who submitted an item decide its exception.

title: Protect sign-in
statement: Sign in with a security key or passkey, or through the customer's identity provider, and never share credentials.
complements: OpenClear supports FIDO2 security keys and passkeys, and the customer's own identity provider.

title: Look after the customer's API credentials
statement: Rotate the customer's API client secrets (or use key pairs), keep them out of source code and shared drives, and revoke a client when its system is retired.
complements: OpenClear shows each secret only once, stores only its hash, and supports key pairs.

title: Send every issued check
statement: Send OpenClear every check the customer issues, and every void, before the check can be presented, complete and accurate (serial, amount, date, and payee where the bank matches payees).
complements: OpenClear matches presented items against what the customer sent, and raises an exception for anything that differs.
csf: ID.RA-09; PR.DS-01; PR.DS-02; PR.DS-10; PR.PS-02; DE.CM-09

title: Correct rejected rows
statement: Review each upload's result and correct or resubmit any rejected rows the same business day.
complements: OpenClear validates every row, rejects what it can't match on, and says why.

title: Review statements promptly
statement: Examine bank statements and paid items with reasonable promptness, and report any unauthorized or altered item to the bank at once (UCC 4-406).
complements: OpenClear shows each exception with its deadline, and records what the customer saw and decided.

title: Decide exceptions every day
statement: Review exceptions every business day, decide each before its deadline, and return anything not recognized.
complements: OpenClear raises exceptions with their deadline, reminds before the cutoff, and applies the default disposition otherwise.
csf: ID.RA-01; ID.IM-01; ID.IM-02; ID.IM-03; PR.DS-01; PR.DS-02; PR.DS-10; DE.CM-01; DE.CM-06; DE.CM-09; DE.AE-02; DE.AE-03

title: Keep ACH authorizations current
statement: Keep the ACH debit authorizations (who may debit each account, and up to how much) current, and revoke one when the relationship ends.
complements: OpenClear raises an exception for an ACH debit no authorization covers.

title: Report fraud at once
statement: Report suspected fraud or an unauthorized debit to the bank at once, and complete the bank's statement of unauthorized debit when the bank asks for one (the Nacha Rules require it for consumer accounts).
complements: OpenClear shows the customer the bank's statement form, and returns the debit when the customer decides to.
csf: PR.IR-03; RS.MA-01; RS.MA-02; RS.MA-03; RS.MA-04; RS.AN-06; RS.AN-07; RS.CO-02; RS.CO-03; RC.CO-03

title: Protect what's downloaded
statement: Treat reports, exports and check images downloaded from OpenClear as confidential: store them encrypted, share them only with those who need them, and delete them when no longer needed.
complements: OpenClear limits downloads to the customer's own accounts and records each export.

title: Train against fraud and social engineering
statement: Train the people who issue checks and decide exceptions on check fraud and social engineering, such as fake requests to change payment details or to pay an item.
complements: OpenClear shows the information a decision needs, but can't judge whether the person deciding has been trained.

title: Test integration changes
statement: Test changes to the customer's own integration (issue-file exports, API clients) in the sandbox before using them in production.
complements: OpenClear's sandbox runs the same API and file formats as production.

title: Encrypt storage at rest
statement: Encrypt the database, file storage (check images, uploads, archives) and backups at rest, and record how in OPENCLEAR_STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_ATTESTATION.
complements: OpenClear encrypts stored secrets itself (AES-256-GCM) and shows the host's statement on the Controls page.

title: Manage the keys
statement: Generate the signing keys and the field-encryption key outside the image, keep them in a secret store, restrict who can read them, and rotate them on the host's schedule.
complements: OpenClear refuses to start in production with development keys, versions its encryption key and re-encrypts on rotation.

title: Serve only over HTTPS
statement: Terminate HTTPS with a current certificate and modern TLS in front of OpenClear, and never serve it over plain HTTP.
complements: OpenClear sets secure, SameSite cookies and a strict Content Security Policy.

title: Lock down the origin
statement: Let only the edge network reach OpenClear, keep the database and storage off the internet, and record how the origin is locked down.
complements: OpenClear checks edge headers come from trusted ranges, and accepts an edge secret.

title: Run with production settings
statement: Run production with production settings: real keys, no development defaults, and the scheduled control tests on.
complements: OpenClear checks its own settings at startup and on the Controls page.

title: Back up and test restores
statement: Back up the database and file storage, encrypted and kept apart from the primary, with at least one copy immutable or offline behind sign-in separate from production; state how long backups are kept; and test a clean restore at least yearly.
complements: OpenClear's database migrations upgrade and downgrade, and its action log verifies after a restore.

title: State recovery objectives
statement: State the installation's recovery time and recovery point objectives, record them and each restore test's date in OpenClear's settings, and give the banks the restore tests' results.
complements: OpenClear shows them on every bank's Controls page, and warns when they're missing or the test is over a year old.
csf: ID.IM-01; ID.IM-02; ID.IM-03; ID.IM-04; PR.IR-02; PR.IR-03; RC.RP-03; RC.CO-04

title: Apply updates
statement: Apply OpenClear releases, and operating system, database and dependency patches, within the host's patching deadlines.
complements: OpenClear publishes versioned releases with a changelog, and shows the running version.

title: Scan for vulnerabilities
statement: Scan the servers, container images and database for vulnerabilities, and fix what's found within the host's deadlines.
complements: OpenClear's source and dependencies are public for anyone to scan.
csf: GV.SC-10; ID.RA-01; ID.RA-08; ID.IM-01; ID.IM-02; ID.IM-03

title: Limit administrative access to the host
statement: Limit access to the servers, database and secret store to named administrators using a second factor, and log it. Platform staff reach a bank's data only through the bank's support access grants.
complements: OpenClear gives platform staff no way into a bank except a grant the bank makes.
where: Support access; the host's access records

nist_title: Store on Separate Physical Systems or Components
title: Keep logs off the host
statement: Send the installation's security events and logs to a system the application's administrators can't change, and keep action-log archives in write-once storage.
complements: OpenClear signs and chains the action log, and delivers security events to the installation's destination.

title: Watch that it's running
statement: Monitor /health, the job queue and the scheduled jobs, and alert someone when they stop.
complements: OpenClear reports its health and each scheduled job's last run.

title: Notify banks of incidents
statement: Issue an incident notice in OpenClear (Platform → Incidents) to each affected bank as soon as possible after determining an incident that has disrupted or degraded its service, or is likely to, for four hours or more (12 CFR 304.24), or a cybersecurity event affecting its systems or data (23 NYCRR 500.11(b)(3)), and follow the runbook's Incidents section.
complements: OpenClear emails each bank's incident contacts, shows the notice until the bank acknowledges it, and records both.

where: Platform → Incidents; the host's incident records

title: Notify banks of unauthorized access to their customers' information
statement: Notify each affected bank as soon as possible of unauthorized access to its customer information, whether or not it disrupted the service, with what the logs show was reached (12 CFR 364 App. B Supplement A).
complements: OpenClear's action log records who viewed check images and who exported data, so the reach can be shown.

title: Screen the host's staff
statement: Screen everyone with access to the installation or to banks' data before granting it, as the banks' contracts require (12 CFR 364 App. B III.C.1.e).
complements: OpenClear gives platform staff no way into a bank except a grant the bank makes, and logs what they do.

title: Keep an incident response plan
statement: Keep an incident response and recovery plan for the installation (roles, decisions, communications with the banks, root cause), and test it each year.
complements: OpenClear's runbook has an Incidents section to build the plan on.
csf: ID.IM-01; ID.IM-02; ID.IM-03; ID.IM-04; PR.IR-03; DE.AE-03; DE.AE-08; RS.MA-01; RS.MA-05; RS.AN-08; RC.RP-01; RC.RP-02; RC.RP-04; RC.RP-06

title: Train the host's staff
statement: Give everyone with access to the installation security awareness training, including social engineering, at least yearly.
complements: OpenClear limits platform staff to what their role allows and logs what they do.

title: Test penetration yearly
statement: Have a qualified party penetration-test the installation at least yearly, and share the summary with the banks.
complements: OpenClear's security metrics, advisories and ASVS crosswalk are published with each release.

title: Delete a bank's data when it leaves
statement: When a bank leaves, offboard it in OpenClear (Platform → the bank's Offboarding) as the contract says, send the bank the signed deletion certificate, and tell it how long the host's backups keep copies.
complements: OpenClear tells the bank to take its final export, deletes every row and file of the bank after a wait and two operators' approval, and signs a certificate of what was deleted.
where: Platform → the bank's Offboarding; the deletion certificate

title: Announce maintenance
statement: Announce scheduled maintenance and upgrades to each bank beforehand, as a maintenance notice in OpenClear, so they aren't incidents under 12 CFR 304.24(b).
complements: OpenClear sends maintenance notices the same way as incident notices.
